questions.text:
An IT technician is working on a support ticket regarding an unreachable website. The technician has utilized the ping command to the website, but the site is still unreachable.
Which of the following tools should the technician use NEXT?
questions.explanation: Tracert shows the path packets take and identifies where connectivity fails along the route to the website. Netstat displays local connection statistics, not path information needed for this issue.

questions.text:
An ISP configured an internet connection to provide 20Mbps, but actual data rates are occurring at 10Mbps and causing a significant delay in data transmission.
Which of the following specifications should the ISP check?
questions.explanation: Throughput measures the actual data transfer rate achieved, which is what's underperforming compared to the provisioned bandwidth. Bandwidth refers to the maximum theoretical capacity, which was already confirmed at 20Mbps.

questions.text:
An application team is deploying a new application. The application team would like the network team to monitor network performance and create alerts if fluctuations in the round-trip time occur for that traffic.
Which of the following should the network team monitor to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Latency measures round-trip time for traffic, directly matching the requirement to monitor fluctuations in round-trip time. Bandwidth measures capacity, not timing of packet delivery.

questions.text:
A network administrator is configuring Neighbor Discovery Protocol in an IPv6 network to ensure an attacker cannot spoof link-layer addresses of network devices.
Which of the following should the administrator implement?
questions.explanation: Router Advertisement Guard (RA Guard) protects against spoofed link-layer/router advertisements in IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Protocol, preventing rogue or spoofed advertisements. MAC filtering and port security operate at Layer 2 but don't specifically address Neighbor Discovery Protocol spoofing.

questions.text:
A network architect is developing documentation for an upcoming IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack implementation. The architect wants to shorten the following IPv6 address: ef82:0000:0000:0000:0000:1ab1:1234:1bc2.
Which of the following is the MOST appropriate shortened version?
questions.explanation: Consecutive all-zero groups can be replaced once with '::', and leading zeros dropped, giving ef82::1ab1:1234:1bc2. The other options either omit required groups or misuse double colon placement.

questions.text: Which of the following default ports is MOST likely used to send availability and environmental messages about specific devices across the network?
questions.explanation: Syslog, used for logging device status and environmental alerts, uses UDP/TCP port 514 by default. Port 53 is DNS and 389 is LDAP, neither related to device logging.

questions.text:
A newly installed multifunction copier needs to be set up so scanned documents can be emailed to recipients.
Which of the following ports from the copier’s IP address should be allowed?
questions.explanation: Scan-to-email functionality requires SMTP, which uses port 25 by default. Port 80 is HTTP and unrelated to sending mail.

questions.text: Which of the following has the capability to centrally manage configuration, logging, and firmware versioning for distributed devices?
questions.explanation: A WLAN controller centrally pushes configuration, collects logs, and manages firmware images for all its distributed access points. A SIEM only aggregates and correlates log data; it does not configure devices or manage firmware versions.

questions.text:
A PC on the company network is experiencing connectivity issues, and a help desk technician is attempting to resolve the issue. The technician plans to run a constant ping command from a Windows workstation while testing various possible reasons for the connectivity issue.
Which of the following should the technician use?
questions.explanation: The -t switch causes ping to run continuously until manually stopped, ideal for ongoing connectivity testing. The -w switch sets a timeout, not continuous pinging.

questions.text: Which of the following is the MOST effective security control to keep a company’s physical perimeter protected against intrusions leveraged by social-engineering techniques?
questions.explanation: The question asks for the most effective control protecting the physical perimeter; an access control vestibule physically prevents tailgating and piggybacking by allowing only one person through at a time. Training influences behavior but does not physically stop an intruder from following someone in.

questions.text:
A customer called the help desk to report a network issue. The customer recently added a hub between the switch and the router in order to duplicate the traffic flow to a logging device. After adding the hub, all the other network components that were connected to the switch slowed more than expected.
Which of the following is the MOST likely cause of the issue?
questions.explanation: Hubs operate in half duplex, so connecting one to a full-duplex switch port creates a duplex mismatch, causing collisions and degraded performance for all connected devices. STP malfunction wouldn't cause gradual slowdowns tied to hub insertion.

questions.text:
A fiber patch cable, which was being stored in an unsecure telecommunications closet with janitorial supplies, was damaged and caused an outage. A network technician replaced the broken cable with a new cable from a sealed bag. However, this solution did not resolve the outage.
Which of the following is the MOST likely explanation?
questions.explanation: When a fiber patch cable is swapped, the most common installer error is connecting transmit to transmit and receive to receive, leaving the link down. A factory-sealed cable with capped connectors is unlikely to be contaminated, and pinout issues apply to copper.

questions.text:
An engineer is gathering data to determine the effectiveness of UPSs in use at remote retail locations.
Which of the following statistics can the engineer use to determine the availability of the remote network equipment?
questions.explanation: Uptime directly measures how long equipment remains operational and available, which reflects the effectiveness of UPS backup power. NetFlow baselines and interface statistics measure traffic patterns, not availability.

questions.text:
A technician uses a badge to enter a security checkpoint on a corporate campus. An unknown individual quickly walks in behind the technician without speaking.
Which of the following types of attacks did the technician experience?
questions.explanation: Tailgating occurs when an unauthorized person follows an authorized individual through a secured entry without permission or acknowledgment. Piggybacking implies the authorized person knowingly allows entry, which isn't described here.

questions.text:
A company is opening a new building on the other side of its campus. The distance from the closest building to the new building is 1,804ft (550m). The company needs to connect the networking equipment in the new building to the other buildings on the campus without using a repeater.
Which of the following transceivers should the company use?
questions.explanation: 10GBASE-LR supports single-mode fiber distances up to 10km without repeaters, easily covering 550m. 10GBASE-SR and 10GBASE-SW are multimode standards limited to much shorter distances.

questions.text:
An AP uses a 98ft (30m) Cat 6 cable to connect to an access switch. The cable is wired through a duct close to a three-phase motor installation. Anytime the three-phase is turned on, all users connected to the switch experience high latency on the network.
Which of the following is MOST likely the cause of the issue?
questions.explanation: Three-phase motors generate strong electromagnetic fields that induce interference (EMI) into nearby copper cabling, degrading signal quality and causing latency. Attenuation relates to signal loss over distance, not equipment-triggered noise.

questions.text:
An IT technician installs five old switches in a network. In addition to the low port rates on these switches, they also have improper network configurations. After three hours, the network becomes overwhelmed by continuous traffic and eventually shuts down.
Which of the following is causing the issue?
questions.explanation: Old switches with improper configuration (e.g., no STP) can create loops that generate excessive broadcast traffic, overwhelming the network—a broadcast storm. Collisions alone wouldn't cause a total shutdown over time.

questions.text:
An engineer is designing a network topology for a company that maintains a large on-premises private cloud. A design requirement mandates internet-facing hosts to be partitioned off from the internal LAN and internal server IP ranges.
Which of the following defense strategies helps meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: A screened subnet (DMZ) isolates internet-facing hosts from the internal LAN and servers while still allowing controlled access. A honeypot is a decoy system, not a segmentation strategy.

questions.text:
Many IP security cameras use RTSP to control media playback.
Which of the following default transport layer port numbers does RTSP use?
questions.explanation: RTSP uses TCP/UDP port 554 by default for streaming media control. Port 5060 is used by SIP, not RTSP.

questions.text: Which of the following would be increased by adding encryption to data communication across the network?
questions.explanation: Encryption protects data from unauthorized viewing, directly increasing confidentiality. It does not inherently ensure data integrity, which relies on hashing or checksums.

questions.text:
A network technician is working at a new office location and needs to connect one laptop to another to transfer files. The laptops are newer models and do not have Ethernet ports. Access points are not available either.
Which of the following types of wireless network SSIDs does the network technician need to configure to be able to connect the laptops together?
questions.explanation: An Independent Basic Service Set (ad hoc network) allows two wireless devices to connect directly without an access point. A Basic Service Set requires an access point to coordinate communication.

questions.text:
An organization would like to implement a disaster recovery strategy that does not require a facility agreement or idle hardware.
Which of the following strategies MOST likely meets the organization’s requirements?
questions.explanation: A cloud site leverages cloud infrastructure on demand, avoiding the need for a dedicated facility agreement or idle standby hardware. A cold, warm, or hot site all require a physical facility reserved in advance.

questions.text:
A network administrator is investigating reports about network performance and finds high utilization on a switch uplink. The administrator is unsure whether this is an anomaly or normal behavior that will require an upgrade to resolve.
Which of the following should the administrator reference to gain historical perspective?
questions.explanation: A network performance baseline provides historical data to compare against current utilization and determine whether current traffic levels are abnormal. An SLA defines expected service levels but doesn't provide historical performance trends.

questions.text:
A network administrator is troubleshooting a client’s device that cannot connect to the network. A physical inspection of the switch shows the RJ45 is connected. The NIC shows no activity lights. The network administrator moves the device to another location and connects to the network without issues.
Which of the following tools would be the BEST option for the network administrator to use to further troubleshoot?
questions.explanation: Since the device works elsewhere, a cable tester can verify whether the original cable run itself is faulty, such as a wiring or continuity issue. A tone generator is for tracing cable paths, not verifying signal integrity.

questions.text:
A non-employee was able to enter a server room.
Which of the following could have prevented this from happening?
questions.explanation: A biometric reader provides strong physical access control that would prevent unauthorized entry into a server room, whereas a camera only records events without preventing entry.

questions.text:
A large number of PCs are obtaining an APIPA IP address, and a number of new computers were added to the network.
Which of the following is MOST likely causing the PCs to obtain an APIPA address?
questions.explanation: APIPA addresses appear when clients cannot obtain a lease, and with many new computers added, the DHCP scope is most likely exhausted. A rogue DHCP server would typically hand out wrong but valid addresses, not cause APIPA fallback.

questions.text:
An engineer is using a tool to run an ICMP sweep of a network to find devices that are online. When reviewing the results, the engineer notices a number of workstations that are currently verified as being online are not listed in the report. The tool was configured to scan using the following information:
Network address: 172.28.16.0 -CIDR: /22 -The engineer collected the following information from the client workstation:
IP address: 172.28.17.206 -Subnet mask: 255.255.252.0 -
Which of the following MOST likely explains why the tool is failing to detect some workstations?
options: The scanned network range is incorrect.
The subnet mask on the client is misconfigured.
The workstation has a firewall enabled.
The tool is unable to scan remote networks.
questions.explanation: The scanner was configured for the /22 range 172.28.16.0-172.28.19.255, but the actual workstation VLAN spans a /20 (172.28.16.0-172.28.31.255), so hosts like 172.28.20.31, 172.28.22.17, and 172.28.27.88 fall outside the scanned range and are missed. The client's subnet mask matches the site's addressing plan, so it is not misconfigured.

questions.text: Which of the following can be used to limit the ability of devices to perform only HTTPS connections to an internet update server without exposing the devices to the public internet?
options: Allow connections only to an internal proxy server.
Deploy an IDS system and place it in line with the traffic.
Create a screened network and move the devices to it.
Use a host-based network firewall on each device.
questions.explanation: Routing all update traffic through an internal proxy server restricts devices to HTTPS-only outbound connections without giving them direct public internet exposure. A screened network (DMZ) would still expose devices more directly to external traffic.

questions.text:
A network administrator notices excessive wireless traffic occurring on an access point after normal business hours. The access point is located on an exterior wall.
Which of the following should the administrator do to limit wireless access outside the building?
questions.explanation: Switching to a directional antenna focuses the wireless signal inward, reducing propagation outside the building. Disabling SSID broadcast or roaming does not limit physical signal range.

questions.text:
A technician thinks one of the router ports is flapping.
Which of the following available resources should the technician use in order to determine if the router is flapping?
questions.explanation: Syslog captures system events like interface up/down messages that indicate port flapping. NetFlow tracks traffic flow statistics, not interface state changes.

questions.text: Which of the following layers is where TCP/IP port numbers identify which network application is receiving the packet and where it is applied?
questions.explanation: Port numbers are used at Layer 4 (Transport layer) of the OSI model to identify the receiving application. Layer 3 (Network) handles IP addressing, not ports.

questions.text:
A user reports that a crucial fileshare is unreachable following a network upgrade that was completed the night before. A network technician confirms the problem exists.
Which of the following troubleshooting steps should the network technician perform NEXT?
options: Establish a theory of probable cause.
Implement a solution to fix the problem.
Create a plan of action to resolve the problem.
Document the problem and the solution.
questions.explanation: After identifying the problem, the next step in the troubleshooting methodology is to establish a theory of probable cause. Implementing a solution comes only after testing that theory.

questions.text:
A network engineer is designing a wireless network that has the following requirements:

• Network speed must be higher than 100Mbps
• Must use the 2.4GHz and 5GHz bands

Which of the following 802.11 standards should the engineer select?
questions.explanation: 802.11n supports both 2.4GHz and 5GHz bands and offers speeds well above 100Mbps. 802.11a, b, and g are limited to single bands and/or lower speeds.

questions.text:
A network engineer is investigating reports of poor performance on a videoconferencing application. Upon reviewing the report, the engineer finds that available bandwidth at the WAN connection is low.
Which of the following is the MOST appropriate mechanism to handle this issue?
questions.explanation: Traffic shaping prioritizes bandwidth for critical applications like videoconferencing when WAN bandwidth is limited. Flow control manages data flow between devices, not bandwidth allocation for specific applications.

questions.text: Which of the following protocols can be routed?
questions.explanation: iSCSI runs over standard IP networks and can be routed. NetBEUI and Fibre Channel are non-routable, and FCoE is designed for Layer 2 Ethernet, not routed IP networks.

questions.text:
A Fortune 500 company would like to move its on-premises corporate email systems to a multitenant product hosted in the cloud where no maintenance of the underlying server OS or platform is required.
Which of the following BEST represents the model the company should choose?
questions.explanation: A multitenant, cloud-hosted email product with no OS/platform maintenance describes a public cloud SaaS model. Private cloud would involve dedicated infrastructure, not multitenancy.

questions.text: Which of the following situations would require an engineer to configure subinterfaces?
options: In a router-on-a-stick deployment with multiple VLANs
In order to enable inter-VLAN routing on a multilayer switch
When configuring VLAN trunk links between switches
After connecting a router that does not support 802.1Q VLAN tags
questions.explanation: Router-on-a-stick deployments require subinterfaces on a single physical interface to handle routing between multiple VLANs. Multilayer switches use switched virtual interfaces instead of subinterfaces for inter-VLAN routing.

questions.text: At which of the following OSI model layers does a MAC filter list for a wireless infrastructure operate?
questions.explanation: MAC filtering operates at the Data Link layer since it filters based on MAC addresses, which are Layer 2 identifiers. The Physical layer deals with signals, not addressing.

questions.text:
The Chief Executive Officer of a company wants to ensure business operations are not disrupted in the event of a disaster. The solution must have fully redundant equipment, real-time synchronization, and zero data loss.
Which of the following should be prepared?
questions.explanation: A hot site provides fully redundant, synchronized equipment for zero data loss and immediate failover. A warm site has some equipment but lacks real-time synchronization needed for zero data loss.

questions.text:
An IT technician needs to increase bandwidth to a server. The server has multiple gigabit ports.
Which of the following can be used to accomplish this without replacing hardware?
questions.explanation: LACP (Link Aggregation Control Protocol) combines multiple gigabit ports into a single logical link to increase bandwidth without new hardware. STP prevents loops but doesn't add bandwidth.

questions.text:
A company wants to mitigate unauthorized physical connectivity after implementing a hybrid work schedule.
Which of the following will the company MOST likely configure?
questions.explanation: Port security restricts which devices can physically connect to switch ports by limiting or specifying allowed MAC addresses, preventing unauthorized physical connectivity. DHCP snooping addresses rogue DHCP servers, not physical connection control.

questions.text:
A customer cannot reach a web application on a local server. The network consultant suspects that the server is not accepting the HTTPS connection.
Which of the following commands should the consultant run on the server to determine what is occurring?
questions.explanation: Netstat shows active connections and listening ports on the server, revealing whether the HTTPS port is open and accepting connections. Nmap is typically run from a remote host to scan ports, not locally to check the server's own listening state.

questions.text:
A help desk technician is troubleshooting a Windows server named SQL.local and wants to check which port a specific application is running on.
Which of the following commands should the technician run?
questions.explanation: Netstat displays active connections and the ports applications are using on a Windows server. Dig and traceroute are used for DNS lookups and path tracing, not port usage.

questions.text:
A network administrator is configuring a static DSL connection on the perimeter router to use a backup route to the fiber connection using OSPF routing. The administrator notices all traffic is going over the DSL connection and both links are working.
Which of the following should the administrator do to adjust the routing settings for the fiber connection to be used by the router?
options: Add the DSL connection to the neighbor table for OSPF protocol
Change the routing protocol to EIGRP for the fiber connection
Increase the administrative distance of the DSL connection
Create a separate VLAN for the DSL connection
questions.explanation: Increasing the administrative distance of the DSL route makes it less preferred, allowing OSPF to prefer the fiber connection as the primary path. Adding DSL to the OSPF neighbor table wouldn't affect route preference.

questions.text:
A Chief Information Officer wants to monitor network breaching in a passive, controlled manner.
Which of the following would be BEST to implement?
questions.explanation: A honeypot is a decoy system used to passively observe and study attacker behavior in a controlled environment without disrupting production. An IPS actively blocks threats rather than passively monitoring, and port security only restricts MAC addresses on switchports.

questions.text:
A technician monitors a switch interface and notices it is not forwarding frames on a trunked port. However, the cable and interfaces are in working order.
Which of the following is MOST likely the cause of the issue?
questions.explanation: A trunked port carries tagged VLAN traffic using 802.1Q; a mismatch or misconfiguration of this protocol between switches would prevent frame forwarding despite good physical connectivity. STP would block ports rather than fail silently, and flow control or frame size wouldn't stop all forwarding on a trunk.

questions.text:
A wireless network technician is receiving reports from some users who are unable to see both of the corporate SSIDs on their mobile devices. A site survey was recently commissioned, and the results verified acceptable RSSI from both APs in all user areas. The APs support modern wireless standards and are all broadcasting their SSIDs. The following table shows some of the current AP settings:
Which of the following changes would result in all of the user devices being capable of seeing both corporate SSIDs?
options: Implementing the WPA2 Enterprise authentication standard
Implementing omnidirectional antennas for both APs
Configuring the highest power settings for both APs
Configuring both APs to use the 802.11ac wireless standard
questions.explanation: The only difference between the APs is security: AP2 still uses deprecated WEP/TKIP, which current mobile operating systems no longer support or list, so its SSID never appears. Moving both APs to WPA2 Enterprise fixes it. Both already run 802.11ax, so forcing 802.11ac would change nothing and would drop 2.4 GHz clients.

questions.text:
An infrastructure company is implementing a cabling solution to connect sites on multiple continents.
Which of the following cable types should the company use for this project?
questions.explanation: Single-mode fiber supports the long distances needed for intercontinental connections, typically via undersea cables, due to lower attenuation over long distances. Multimode fiber and copper Cat 6/Cat 7 cannot support such long-distance transmission.

questions.text:
A user is required to log in to a main web application, which then grants the user access to all other programs needed to complete job-related tasks.
Which of the following authentication methods does this setup describe?
questions.explanation: Single sign-on (SSO) allows a user to authenticate once and gain access to multiple applications without re-entering credentials. RADIUS and TACACS+ are AAA protocols, not user-facing login methods, and 802.1X is for network access control.

questions.text:
A company has a geographically remote office. In order to connect to the internet, the company has decided to use a satellite WAN link.
Which of the following is the GREATEST concern for this type of connection?
questions.explanation: Satellite links have very high propagation delay and variable latency, causing significant jitter, which is the greatest concern for real-time traffic. Duplex, collisions, and encapsulation are not primary issues with satellite WAN links.

questions.text:
A network technician is deploying multiple switches for a new office. The switches are separately managed and need to be cabled in to support dual firewalls in a HA setup.
Which of the following should the technician enable to support proper stability of the network switches?
questions.explanation: Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) prevents Layer 2 loops when multiple switches are interconnected for redundancy, ensuring network stability. LACP aggregates links but doesn't prevent loops, and NTP, CDMA, and 802.1Q are unrelated to loop prevention.

questions.text: Which of the following would be used to filter web traffic based on content?
questions.explanation: A proxy server can inspect and filter web traffic based on content, URLs, or categories. Load balancers distribute traffic, media converters change physical media types, and access points provide wireless connectivity, none of which filter content.

questions.text:
A bank installed a new smart TV to stream online video services, but the smart TV was not able to connect to the branch Wi-Fi. The next day, a technician was able to connect the TV to the Wi-Fi, but a bank laptop lost network access at the same time.
Which of the following is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explanation: Connecting a new device likely exhausted the DHCP scope, causing the laptop to lose its IP address lease. Channel overlap or AP reset would not cause simultaneous loss of connectivity tied directly to a new device joining.

questions.text:
Newly crimped 26ft (8m) STP Cat 6 patch cables were recently installed in one room to replace cables that were damaged by a vacuum cleaner. Now, users in that room are unable to connect to the network. A network technician tests the existing cables first. The 177ft (54m) cable that runs from the core switch to the access switch on the floor is working, as is the 115ft (35m) cable run from the access switch to the wall jack in the office.
Which of the following is the MOST likely reason the users cannot connect to the network?
options: Mixed UTP and STP cables are being used.
The patch cables are not plenum rated.
An incorrect pinout on the patch cable is being used.
questions.explanation: Total run is 54m + 35m + 8m = 97m, within the 100m limit, so distance is not the issue; the only new variable is the freshly crimped patch cables, pointing to an incorrect pinout/termination.

questions.text:
While troubleshooting a network outage, a technician discovers symptoms that indicate a patch cable is connecting the core switch to the router. A network engineer confirms the theory is plausible, and the technician tests the cable. The cable passes the test, and the technician properly plugs the cable back into the correct network ports. However, the network outage continues.
Which of the following is the NEXT step the technician should take to troubleshoot the network outage?
options: Continue to work the original theory.
questions.explanation: Since the cable tested fine and the issue persists after correct reconnection, the original theory is disproven, so the technician must establish a new theory of probable cause. Continuing the original theory or moving to verification steps skips proper troubleshooting methodology.

questions.text:
A help desk supervisor discovers the following ticket excerpt while reviewing notes in a customer’s account:

• Received report that customer was unable to use the scanner to read barcodes, the internet no longer worked, and the monitor was fuzzy. Arrived on site and began troubleshooting.
• Confirmed monitor issue. Replaced VGA cable.
• Confirmed scanner failure. Scanner USB cable was unattached. Reattached cable.
• Confirmed internet issue. Duplicated on test laptop. Escalated to ISP.

Which of the following BEST describes what the technician was doing?
options: The technician was questioning the obvious.
The technician was implementing preventative measures.
The technician was approaching multiple problems individually.
The technician was determining if anything had changed.
questions.explanation: The technician addressed the monitor, scanner, and internet problems as separate individual issues rather than assuming one root cause, which describes approaching multiple problems individually. This is not about questioning the obvious or checking for changes specifically.

questions.text: Which of the following routing protocols should be implemented to create a route between a local area network and an ISP?
questions.explanation: BGP is the exterior gateway protocol used to route traffic between autonomous systems, such as between a LAN and an ISP. EIGRP, RIP, and OSPF are interior gateway protocols used within a single autonomous system.

questions.text:
A technician would like to implement a low-latency Wi-Fi network.
Which of the following standards should the technician deploy for the network if the expected user bandwidth is 450Mbps?
questions.explanation: 802.11n supports data rates up to 600Mbps, meeting the 450Mbps requirement with low latency compared to older standards. 802.11a, b, and g offer much lower maximum throughput, insufficient for the stated bandwidth need.

questions.text: Which of the following attacks, if successful, would provide a malicious user who is connected to an isolated guest network access to the corporate network?
questions.explanation: VLAN hopping allows an attacker to send traffic tagged for a different VLAN, potentially reaching the corporate network from an isolated guest VLAN. On-path attacks, IP spoofing, and evil twin attacks don't directly cross VLAN segmentation boundaries.

questions.text:
A network administrator implements a group of access points, only changing the SSID, credentials, and IP address. Shortly after, users begin reporting poor quality and video loss while on video calls in the conference room.
Which of the following should the administrator do to MOST effectively troubleshoot during business hours?
options: Remove the current antennas and replace them with directional antennas on each AP.
Disconnect the AP and move it closer to the conference room.
Configure separate channels on APs that are not supporting the conference room.
Reboot the switch and each AP at the same time.
questions.explanation: Configuring separate, non-overlapping channels on APs near the conference room reduces co-channel interference causing quality issues, and can be done without disrupting service during business hours. Physically moving or rebooting APs would cause outages during work hours.

questions.text:
A desktop support department has observed slow wireless speeds for a new line of laptops using the organization's standard image. No other devices have experienced the same issue.
Which of the following should the network administrator recommend troubleshooting FIRST to resolve this issue?
options: Changing the protocol associated to the SSID
questions.explanation: Since only the new laptop image is affected while other devices work fine, outdated or incompatible wireless drivers in the image are the most likely cause and should be checked first. Signal power, new WAPs, or protocol changes would affect all devices, not just the new laptops.

questions.text:
A technician needs to change an incoming fiber line into an RJ45 copper connection for uplinking a new switch.
Which of the following would BEST satisfy this requirement?
questions.explanation: A media converter changes the signal type between fiber and copper Ethernet (RJ45), allowing the fiber line to connect to a switch's copper uplink port. SFPs convert fiber to a compatible transceiver format but don't provide an RJ45 port; punchdown blocks and F-type connectors are unrelated.

questions.text:
A new engineer at a company is working to understand the network.
Which of the following diagrams should the engineer review to understand the paths traffic takes?
questions.explanation: A logical diagram shows how data flows and is routed through the network, including IP addressing and VLANs, illustrating the paths traffic takes. Physical, wiring, and rack diagrams show hardware placement and physical connections, not traffic flow.

questions.text:
A network technician is attempting to increase throughput by configuring link port aggregation between a Gigabit Ethernet distribution switch and a Fast Ethernet access switch.
Which of the following is the BEST choice concerning speed and duplex for all interfaces that are participating in the link aggregation?
questions.explanation: Since the access switch only supports Fast Ethernet, all aggregated interfaces must match at Full duplex and 100Mb speed to function properly together, as link aggregation requires matching speed and duplex settings. Using 1GB speed settings would exceed the access switch's Fast Ethernet capability.

questions.text:
A junior network engineer is trying to change the native network ID to a non-default value that can then be applied consistently throughout the network environment.
Which of the following issues is the engineer attempting to prevent?
questions.explanation: Changing the native VLAN from its default value helps prevent VLAN hopping attacks that exploit default native VLAN settings for double tagging. DDoS, ARP spoofing, and rogue DHCP are unrelated to native VLAN configuration.

questions.text: Which of the following BEST prevents unauthorized access to spare workstation inventory?
questions.explanation: A locking cabinet physically secures spare inventory from unauthorized removal, while security cameras and tamper detection only monitor or alert but do not prevent access.

questions.text:
A technician is troubleshooting network connectivity from a wall jack. Readings from a multimeter indicate extremely low ohmic values instead of the rated impedance from the switchport.
Which of the following is the MOST likely cause of this issue?
questions.explanation: Extremely low ohmic values indicate a short circuit in the cabling rather than the rated impedance, since a short creates a near-zero resistance path. Faulty LEDs or transceivers would not affect ohmic readings from a multimeter.

questions.text:
A user is experimenting with audio transmissions and would like the transmissions to reach several specific devices simultaneously over the IP network. The user requests assistance from a network technician to configure the appropriate features within the SOHO.
Which of the following should the technician configure to meet the requirements?
questions.explanation: Multicast delivers data to multiple specific devices simultaneously over IP, matching the requirement. Unicast targets a single device and broadcast sends to all devices on the network, neither of which fits selective group delivery.

questions.text:
A retail store recently acquired the store next door. The owners would like this store to support Gigabit Ethernet for up to 328ft (100m).
Which of the following is the MOST cost-effective solution?
questions.explanation: Cat 5e supports Gigabit Ethernet up to 100 meters and is the least expensive option that meets the requirement. Cat 6 and Cat 7 exceed the needed specification at higher cost.

questions.text: Which of the following attacks becomes more effective because of global leakages of users’ passwords?
questions.explanation: Dictionary attacks use lists of known/leaked passwords, so global password leaks make these attacks far more effective by supplying real-world credentials to try. Brute-force attacks instead try all possible combinations rather than relying on known passwords.

questions.text:
A network administration team for a medium-sized business has decided to segment the network, logically separating the finance and marketing teams in order to improve performance for both teams. The finance and marketing teams still need to access resources across the subnets, and the router has a single interface.
Which of the following should the administrator configure in order to allow the traffic?
questions.explanation: Subinterfaces on a single router interface allow router-on-a-stick configuration, enabling inter-VLAN routing between the finance and marketing subnets. Port address translation and classless masking don't provide inter-subnet routing.

questions.text:
A network requirement calls for the network traffic of a specific department within a campus network to be monitored. The network has users from each department located in multiple buildings.
Which of the following should be configured to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: 802.1Q tagging identifies the department's VLAN traffic across buildings, and port mirroring copies that traffic to a monitoring port for analysis. MDIX and flow control relate to cable auto-sensing and congestion control, not traffic monitoring.

questions.text:
A wireless technician is working to upgrade the wireless infrastructure for a company. The company currently uses the 802.11g wireless standard on all access points. The company requires backward compatibility and is requesting the least expensive solution.
Which of the following should the technician recommend to the company?
questions.explanation: 802.11n is backward compatible with 802.11g and is less expensive than newer standards like 802.11ac or 802.11ax. 802.11a operates on a different, incompatible frequency band with 802.11g.

questions.text:
An employee walked into a secure facility and allowed a newly hired employee to walk in as well.
Which of the following is the BEST solution to prevent this from happening again?
questions.explanation: Awareness training teaches employees to recognize and prevent tailgating incidents going forward. A sign alone doesn't ensure compliance, and logs or cameras only record the event after it happens rather than preventing it.

questions.text:
A network administrator is assisting a user who is unable to access network services by using hostname on Host 1. Another user in the same office is able to access the network services with no issue on Host 2. The network administrator runs a command on the affected machine and the working machine and compares the following output:
Which of the follow should the network administrator change to restore connectivity?
options: Change the default gateway on Host 1 to 192.168.1.1.
Change the IPv4 address on Host 2 to 192.168.0.112.
Reconfigure the subnet masks on both hosts.
Update the DNS server on Host 1 to 192.168.0.53.
questions.explanation: Both hosts share the same 192.168.0.0/24 subnet and the 192.168.0.1 gateway, so only the DNS entry differs: Host 1 points to 192.168.1.53 instead of the working 192.168.0.53, which breaks name resolution. Changing the gateway to 192.168.1.1 would put it outside Host 1's subnet and break everything.

questions.text: Which of the following VPN types provides the highest security for a user who travels often but also has the highest bandwidth requirements to provide a satisfactory user experience?
questions.explanation: A full-tunnel VPN encrypts all traffic providing the highest security, at the cost of higher bandwidth usage since all traffic routes through the VPN. Split-tunnel reduces bandwidth but only secures part of the traffic, lowering security.

questions.text:
A technician needs to map the path of a PC to the router.
Which of the following tools should the technician use to accomplish this task?
questions.explanation: Traceroute maps the hop-by-hop path packets take to a destination, showing the route to the router. Ping only tests reachability and round-trip time, not the path.

questions.text:
A company is using a DHCP server with 12-hour leases for its device configurations. A user records the information that the DHCP server provides and uses the information to connect a device with a manual IP set. Over time, the user experiences intermittent connectivity and recurring connection timeouts.
Which of the following is the MOST likely cause of the issue?
options: A duplicate IP address is on the network.
The user's device is pointing to an incorrect DNS server.
The device is set to use an incorrect subnet.
The device is set to use an incorrect gateway.
questions.explanation: Manually setting an IP address that was previously leased via DHCP risks that address being reassigned to another device when the lease expires, causing a duplicate IP address conflict and intermittent connectivity. Incorrect DNS or gateway settings would cause more consistent, not intermittent, issues.

questions.text:
A technician is concerned about unauthorized personnel moving assets that are installed in a data center server rack. The technician installs a networked sensor that sends an alert when the server rack door is opened.
Which of the following did the technician install?
questions.explanation: A networked sensor that alerts when a rack door opens is a tamper detection mechanism, protecting against unauthorized physical access. Cipher locks and access control vestibules are physical barriers, not alerting sensors.

questions.text:
An administrator is preparing an organization for a potential disaster. The administrator configures the network switches and turns off the equipment in a data center.
Which of the following is this scenario an example of?
questions.explanation: A cold site has basic infrastructure like configured switches but equipment powered off until needed during a disaster, matching the scenario. A hot site would have fully operational, running equipment ready for immediate failover.

questions.text: Which of the following is used to require network devices to authenticate before gaining access to a LAN?
questions.explanation: 802.1X provides port-based network access control, requiring device authentication before granting LAN access. 802.1Q handles VLAN tagging, not authentication.

questions.text: Which of the following routing protocols is BEST suited for use on a perimeter router?
questions.explanation: BGP is the standard exterior gateway protocol used on perimeter routers to exchange routes between different autonomous systems, such as connecting to an ISP. OSPF, RIPv2, and EIGRP are interior gateway protocols used within a single autonomous system.

questions.text:

Which of the following configurations on the PC is incorrect?
questions.explanation: The 255.255.255.192 mask limits the PC to 192.168.8.0-63, so 192.168.8.129 falls outside and the PC cannot reach it, while the gateway 192.168.8.1 still answers. The IPv4 address is fine "- it matches the reachable gateway; widening the mask to 255.255.255.0 restores access.

questions.text: Which of the following layers of the OSI model lies between the session layer and the network layer?
questions.explanation: The OSI model orders Layer 5 session, Layer 4 transport, and Layer 3 network, so transport sits between session and network. Presentation is Layer 6, which lies above the session layer, not below it.

questions.text: Which of the following describes a network in which users and devices need to mutually authenticate before any network resource can be accessed?
questions.explanation: Zero trust requires continuous mutual verification of users and devices before granting access to any resource, regardless of network location. Least privilege and need to know instead limit the scope of access rather than requiring mutual authentication.

questions.text:
A technician is setting up DNS records on local servers for the company's cloud DNS to enable access by hostname.
Which of the following records should be used?
questions.explanation: An A record maps a hostname to an IPv4 address, which is what enables clients to reach the servers by name. A CNAME only aliases one name to another and still requires an underlying A record to resolve to an address.

questions.text:
A network administrator responds to a support ticket that was submitted by a customer who is having issues connecting to a website inside of the company network. The administrator verifies that the customer could not connect to a website using a URL.
Which of the following troubleshooting steps would be BEST for the administrator to take?
options: Attempt to connect to the site via IP address.
questions.explanation: Attempting to connect via IP address isolates whether the issue is DNS-related or a true connectivity problem, a basic and quick troubleshooting step. Checking certificates or NTP is premature before confirming basic connectivity.

questions.text:
A network administrator is creating a subnet for a remote office that has 53 network devices. An additional requirement is to use the most efficient subnet.
Which of the following CIDR notations indicates the appropriate number of IP addresses with the LEAST amount of unused addresses?
questions.explanation: A /26 provides 62 usable addresses, enough for 53 devices with the least waste; /24 wastes far too many addresses, and /28 only provides 14 usable addresses, which is insufficient.

questions.text:
A Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of a company purchases a new phone that will be used while traveling to different countries. The CEO needs to be able to place outgoing calls and receive incoming calls on the phone using a SIM card.
Which of the following cellular technologies does the CEO’s phone need?
questions.explanation: GSM is the international cellular standard using SIM cards for identification and roaming across countries. CDMA does not use SIM cards for authentication in the same way and is not as globally compatible.

questions.text:
A network technician is troubleshooting a connection to a local server and has verified that the RDP service is running on the server. After running a command, the technician receives the following output:
Which of the following MOST likely describes the issue?
options: A host-based firewall on the server is blocking the connection.
Too many collisions are occurring on the network segment.
A DoS attack is occurring locally.
A routing loop is in the network.
questions.explanation: Port 3389 shows filtered while 80 and 445 are open, meaning the RDP probes are silently dropped rather than refused "- typical of a host-based firewall rule. Collisions would show packet loss and retransmissions, but the ping reports 0% loss with 1 ms responses and a normal TTL.

questions.text: Which of the following would be used to indicate when unauthorized access to physical internal hardware has occurred?
questions.explanation: A tamper evident seal shows visible signs when a case or device has been opened, indicating unauthorized physical access to internal hardware. Motion detectors and locking racks prevent or detect area access, not internal hardware tampering.

questions.text:
A network technician is investigating a trouble ticket for a user who does not have network connectivity. All patch cables between the wall jacks and computers in the building were upgraded over the weekend from Cat 5 to Cat 6. The newly installed cable is crimped with a TIA/EIA 568A on one end and a TIA/EIA 568B on the other end.
Which of the following should the technician do to MOST likely fix the issue?
options: Ensure the switchport has PoE enabled.
Crimp the cable as a straight-through cable.
Ensure the switchport has STP enabled,
Crimp the cable as a rollover cable.
questions.explanation: Since the cable is wired as a crossover (568A on one end, 568B on the other) instead of straight-through, it should be re-terminated as a straight-through cable for standard patch cable connections to modern auto-MDIX-capable devices. Enabling PoE or STP would not resolve a wiring mismatch.

questions.text: Which of the following is a valid alternative to maintain a deployed proxy technology while saving physical space in the data center by moving the network service to the virtualization infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Network Functions Virtualization (NFV) allows network services like proxies to run as virtualized instances instead of dedicated hardware, saving data center space. SD-WAN addresses WAN path selection, not virtualizing individual network functions.

questions.text:
A network technician wants to identify which DNS servers a computer is configured to use.
Which of the following commands should the technician use?
questions.explanation: The nslookup command can show a computer's configured DNS server along with performing lookups. Netstat and arp show connection and address resolution info, not DNS server configuration.

questions.text: Which of the following routing protocols has routes that are classified with an administrative distance of 110?
questions.explanation: OSPF has a default administrative distance of 110. EIGRP uses 90, RIP uses 120, and BGP uses 20 (external) or 200 (internal).

questions.text: Which of the following focuses on application delivery?
questions.explanation: SaaS (Software as a Service) delivers fully functional applications to end users over the internet. IaaS and PaaS provide infrastructure and platforms respectively, not complete applications.

questions.text:
A network engineer is concerned about VLAN hopping happening on the network.
Which of the following should the engineer do to address this concern?
questions.explanation: Changing the default VLAN (native VLAN) away from VLAN 1 helps prevent VLAN hopping attacks like double-tagging. Private VLANs isolate hosts within a VLAN but do not directly address hopping via trunk misconfiguration.

questions.text:
A network technician receives a support ticket concerning multiple users who are unable to access the company's shared drive. The switch interface that the shared drive is connected to is displaying the following:
Which of the following is MOST likely the issue?
options: The cable is not plugged in.
questions.explanation: The port reports down/down with the notconnect state and no administrative shutdown, meaning no link is detected on the media "- an unplugged or failed cable. If the port had been disabled it would read "administratively down," so the switchport being shut down does not fit.

questions.text:
A customer calls the help desk to report that users are unable to access any network resources. The issue started earlier in the day when an employee rearranged the wiring closet. A technician goes to the site but does not observe any obvious damage. The statistics output on the switch indicates high CPU usage, and all the lights on the switch are blinking rapidly in unison.
Which of the following is the MOST likely explanation for these symptoms?
options: The switch was rebooted and set to run in safe mode.
The line between the switch and the upstream router was removed.
A cable was looped and created a broadcast storm.
A Cat 6 cable from the modem to the router was replaced with Cat 5e.
questions.explanation: Rapid blinking lights in unison and high CPU usage after wiring changes indicate a switching loop causing a broadcast storm, likely from an accidental cable loop. A removed uplink would cause loss of connectivity but not high CPU and simultaneous blinking across all ports.

questions.text:
A network administrator is troubleshooting a PC that cannot connect to the LAN. The administrator runs the ipconfig command at the command prompt and gets the following output:
Which of the following is misconfigured?
questions.explanation: The /28 mask (255.255.255.240) puts this host in 192.168.1.32-47, so the default gateway at 192.168.1.1 is treated as off-net and unreachable, while every other LAN host uses /24. The physical address is a valid MAC, and the DNS server is the gateway itself, so it is not the misconfigured item.
